India thus benefits from a Pakistan that remains a neutral broker, preserving a buffer against a binary Gulf polarity.

Energy realism dominates the calculus. India’s oil basket is 30% Saudi‑sourced, while a growing share arrives from the US and Qatar. Disruption in the Red Sea would elevate freight costs and push India to accelerate LNG imports from the US and the emerging Russian‑Ukrainian corridor—options that align with New Delhi’s diversification agenda. Moreover, Indian firms have deep stakes in Saudi petro‑chemical ventures; a hostile Riyadh could imperil multi‑billion‑dollar projects.

Trade routes through the Gulf of Aden are also critical for India’s maritime commerce. Any escalation risks higher insurance premiums and rerouting, which would erode the cost advantage of Indian exports to Africa and Europe. Hence, India must lobby for an international naval coordination mechanism that guarantees free passage, while quietly expanding its own blue‑water logistics capability.
